\chapter{The Kundur two-area system}\label{doc:ts-kundur}

The Kundur two-area system is the standard benchmark for inter-area oscillation studies: two symmetric areas connected by a weak tie, each with two 900 MVA synchronous generators (11 buses, 4 machines, 60 Hz). The RAMSES implementation uses the Kundur-book machine models with \texttt{exc\_kundur} AVR/PSS and thermal governors, and ships two dynamic data variants, with and without power system stabilizers, so the damping of the inter-area mode can be compared directly.

\textbf{Repository:} \href{https://github.com/SPS-L/stepss-Kundur-Two-Area-System}{SPS-L/stepss-Kundur-Two-Area-System}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\section{Quick Start}\label{ts-kundur:quick-start}

\begin{Verbatim}
import stepss

case = stepss.cfg()
case.addData('lf.dat')            # power-flow data
case.addData('dyn.dat')           # dynamic data (use dyn_noPSS.dat for the no-PSS variant)
case.addData('solveroptions.dat') # solver settings
case.addDst('disturb.dst')        # +0.5 pu load step on L9 at t = 1 s, 60 s horizon
case.addObs('obs.dat')            # observables to record

sim = stepss.sim()
sim.execSim(case)
\end{Verbatim}

Running the same disturbance with \texttt{dyn.dat} and \texttt{dyn\_noPSS.dat} (PSS gain set to zero) demonstrates the poorly damped inter-area oscillation and its stabilization by the PSS.

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}
